problem: Mainstream visual localization relies on dense 3D metric maps (SfM/SLAM, e.g. ~2GB per indoor scene for hLoc) that are costly to store, build and maintain as environments change. Sparse topo-metric maps are lightweight but make metric-level localization hard.
motivation: Robot navigation, especially long-term and large-scale, needs a scalable, easily updated map that still gives metric poses. Recent zero-shot dense feature matchers (MASt3R) make pose estimation from a single reference image feasible, so a sparse image-graph map may suffice for non-safety-critical navigation.
key_idea: Localize coarse-to-fine on a two-level topo-metric graph of keyframe images (VPR retrieval, then MASt3R matching with depth-lifted PnP+RANSAC, then factor-graph pose fusion with odometry) and use it for image-goal navigation.
insight: Zero-shot MASt3R is the most accurate and robust matcher for map-free relocalization from a single reference image, beating RoMa, DUSt3R, LoFTR, LightGlue and XFeat in the matcher benchmark (e.g. 66.19% at [5cm,5°] on sim/UCL, median 0.39m on HKUSTGZ) at ~100 ms. Sparse VLoc poses at 0.5 Hz stay accurate, and fusing them with high-rate odometry corrects drift; with drifty AirSLAM odometry, PS-Opt still cuts error (43.5 to 2.9 m) but stays well above pure VLoc. A map of 81 nodes costs only 17MB for a ~200m route.
method: Two-level topo-metric map: connectivity graph (for planning) and covisibility graph (for VLoc, storing pose, CosPlace descriptors and raw images per node); keyframes are chosen greedily to maximize occupied 2D grid cells (or downsampled point clouds) under a budget M.
Global Localization: pretrained CosPlace (ResNet-18, 256-d descriptor) retrieves the top-1 node to initialize the pose at start or after tracking loss.

Local Localization: finds the closest node from the prior pose, gathers covisible neighbors, picks the most similar reference; MASt3R gives dense 2D-2D matches, which are lifted to 2D-3D with the depth image and fed to PnP+RANSAC, with the inlier count as a success check.

Pose SLAM: factor graph (GTSAM) fusing low-rate VLoc priors with high-rate local odometry (ICP in sim, proprioceptive odometry or AirSLAM in real), optimized upon each new VLoc result and propagated by odometry otherwise.
Image-goal navigation: Dijkstra on the connectivity graph gives subgoal nodes; local planner is iPlanner (sim) or a modified Falco motion-primitive planner (real) using single-frame depth.
New map-free relocalization dataset: simulated Matterport3D, UCL Campus (ANYmal-D) and HKUSTGZ Campus, used to benchmark 13 feature matchers.

setting.backbone: CosPlace (ResNet-18) for VPR + MASt3R for matching (both pretrained, frozen, no fine-tuning); classical PnP/RANSAC and GTSAM
setting.training_data: none (pretrained models used zero-shot; no training done by the authors)
setting.observation: RGB-D (ZED2 stereo camera in the real world, depth up to 15 m) plus local odometry (proprioceptive or ICP/AirSLAM)
setting.action_space: local collision-free paths via iPlanner / Falco motion primitives on ANYmal-D legged robot; subgoals from topological graph
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (with CMU autonomous navigation stack) plus real world
setting.privileged: Map built from geo-tagged images with known poses (GT/SLAM/AR glasses); depth for the query; manually provided initial pose for mapping; GT localization used only for the baseline

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark (only own datasets and custom simulated sequences); metrics are relative pose/ATE and navigation time/path length, which do not match the canonical metric keys, so no entries are listed. Key own results: matcher table (MASt3R on Sim Matterport3D+UCL: median 0.06m/0.64°, [5cm,5°] 66.19, [25cm,5°] 80.75, [1m,10°] 94.83, 97.18% estimated, 101 ms; on HKUSTGZ: median 0.39m/1.05°, 5.39/47.44/74.36, 96.92%, 99 ms); real ATE with RobotOdom-VLoc 0.238/0.217/0.191 m on Seq0-2 (map 17MB+83KB); sim VNav LiteVLoc+iPlanner 50.0s/28.6m, 52.9s/29.1m, 280.3s/223.7m vs GTLoc+Falco 40.3s/25.5m, 42.7s/28.3m, 266.9s/220.7m in Env0-2.
results: MASt3R is the best matcher across datasets, and LiteVLoc reaches ATE of about 0.2 m on 129-198 m real sequences with a 17 MB map, and 0.01-0.07 m in simulation. In simulated image-goal navigation it needs slightly more time (e.g. 50.0s vs 40.3s) but similar path length compared with a GT-localization + Falco baseline, and it completed a 94.5 m real ANYmal-D route in 314 s.
limitations: Assumes the robot always has valid localization and stays inside the mapped region; requires depth for queries, and single-frame depth planning gets stuck in local minima (limited camera FOV, more rotations)

Domain gaps between devices and reference/query images are not addressed; reference selection uses handcrafted hierarchical retrieval; low-rate (0.5 Hz) VLoc with heavy models; evaluation is small-scale with no standard benchmark or success-rate metrics
Odometry drift (e.g. AirSLAM) is only partly corrected by the PS module
